title: TRF: Tri-Lateral Retention Feasibility Model. Executable artefact for EHDS and GDPR audit-log retention and erasure
description:
Executable research artefact for the MSc thesis Verifiable Crypto-Erasure for Cross-Border Health Data Audit Trails under the European Health Data Space (Arshad Akhtar Abbasia, Høgskolen i Molde (Molde University College), Norway, 2026; supervisor Prof. João Ferreira). It accompanies a design science study of how audit logs of cross-border health data exchange can be retained, erased and still verified under Regulation (EU) 2025/327 (EHDS) and Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR).

Research problem. One audit record from cross-border health data exchange (MyHealth@EU, National Contact Points for eHealth) or from a Secure Processing Environment is bound by three obligations at once: a retention floor (Article 73(1)(e) EHDS for access logs; a nationally set period for cross-border audit repositories), the right to erasure (Article 17 GDPR), and the six-month deletion ceiling of Article 68(12) EHDS. No instrument reconciles them.

Contribution. The Tri-Lateral Retention Feasibility (TRF) Model writes the three obligations as constraints over discretised time and makes the semantics of audit verifiability an explicit parameter. If a verifiable record must stay readable, the constraints cannot be met together whenever a deadline falls inside the retention window (Proposition 1; in the generated population, 95 violations across 90 of 200 records, 39 of them with no erasure request at all, Corollary 1.2). If verifiable means accountable (who acted, when, a hiding commitment and a logged invalidation entry), in the model they can always be met (Proposition 2; 0 violations, with 138 records invalidated: 52 on Article 17 and 86 on Article 68(12)). The witnessing mechanism, Crypto-Erasure by Invalidation, destroys each record's payload key at its deadline and appends every event to a Merkle audit log (RFC 6962 hashing) whose inclusion proofs detect an altered entry; detecting a rewritten log needs a published root, which is specified and not implemented.

Contents. Constraint checker (Python standard library); exhaustive cross-check against the checker at every boundary month; bounded Z3 SMT check of Propositions 1 to 3 with mutation tests; AES-256-GCM envelope-encryption module; Synthea FHIR R4 payload layer; Norwegian context modules (Helsedataservice permits, secure processing environments, politiregisterloven § 17); a Streamlit viewer with an examiner's walk and a claim ledger; 56 automated tests run in continuous integration on Python 3.11 to 3.13. Every recorded output that can be re-run from the repository reproduces byte for byte.

Limitations. Results are checked on synthetic data and are not estimates of real frequency. The proofs are informal, checked by code and a bounded SMT search. Key destruction is simulated and attested, not proven. The retained residue is pseudonymised, not anonymous. Two interpretive steps (whether an invalidated record still satisfies a retention obligation, and whether Article 68(12) EHDS reaches access logs kept at patient level) await regulatory authority; the thesis marks which results depend on each.

Intended users. Operators of National Contact Points for eHealth and of Secure Processing Environments, health data access bodies, data protection officers and supervisory authorities preparing for the EHDS implementing acts (requirements for Secure Processing Environments are due by 26 March 2027); researchers in privacy engineering, health informatics and information logistics who want a small, checkable formal model to extend.

How to cite. Abbasia, A. A. (2026). TRF: Tri-Lateral Retention Feasibility Model (Version 1.3.1) [Computer software]. Zenodo. The thesis cites version 1.3.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23989242); no computed figure differs between 1.3.0 and this version. The concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23819274 always resolves to the latest version.

Reproduce. Python 3.11 to 3.13. pip install -r requirements.txt; python3 trf_checker.py prints Semantics I: 95 violations across 90 records, Semantics II: 0, and exits 0 only if Semantics II holds; python3 -m pytest -q tests/ runs the 56 tests. Optional: pip install z3-solver, then python3 z3_check.py. The run is deterministic under seed 20260915; the commitment of record 100 begins 678ade47c1e6dc03, the fastest check that a run is the reported run. No personal data is used or needed.
notes: Norsk: Kjørbar forskningsartefakt til masteroppgaven Verifiable Crypto-Erasure for Cross-Border Health Data Audit Trails under the European Health Data Space ved Høgskolen i Molde (2026). Oppgaven undersøker hvordan revisjonslogger for grensekryssende helsedata kan oppbevares, slettes og fortsatt etterprøves under forordningen om det europeiske helsedataområdet (EHDS, forordning (EU) 2025/327) og personvernforordningen (GDPR artikkel 17). Modellen viser at kravene er uforenlige når en slettefrist faller innenfor lagringsperioden, dersom en logg bare er etterprøvbar så lenge innholdet kan leses, og forenlige i modellen dersom etterprøvbarhet betyr etterrettelighet. Analysen er gjort mot norsk infrastruktur: Helsedirektoratet som nasjonalt kontaktpunkt for e-helse, Helsedataservice og sikre analyserom. Dataene er syntetiske.
